chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no man who withholds a dirham that is his right, except that he will spend two [dirhams] in what is not his right; and there is no man who withholds a right from his wealth, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will make a snake of fire encircle him on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: A silver coin, representing a small amount of money
key_terms.طَوَّقَهُ: He made him wear/encircle (with a collar or chain)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of withholding one's due wealth or rights according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the spiritual penalty of withholding wealth to the concept of *Dahr* (divine spoilage), where a single dirham withheld results in the expenditure of two in futile pursuits. The vivid imagery of a 'snake of fire' around the neck signifies the eternal burden of unfulfilled financial obligations, particularly Zakah, serving as a stern warning against hoarding and neglecting one's fiscal duties to the Imam.
